reviews.title: Barely functional
reviews.text:
For an app that’s meant to teach coding, it sure does have terribly buggy code. Most of the time I load it up it tries to force me to sign up for a plan, even though I’ve already paid for the full year. I have to actually turn my phone off and on to get the app to work, and this has happened 3 times in the 2 days I’ve had it. For learning python it has you enter and run a function but then it just tells you if it was right or wrong, doesn’t actually show the output. And when scoring, it can’t differentiate the count right and count wrong - so if there are two questions and I get 1 correct and 1 incorrect, it shows 2 and 2. If there are 3 questions and I get 2 right and 1 wrong, it shows 3 and 3. 

Absolutely terrible. Feels like vibe coded slop.

reviews.title: Not Really Free
reviews.text: I know you guys wanna make money and all, but there is no way to get credits besides paying, it’s like a worse version of a free trial and I haven’t even passed 4 lessons, just now logging on after like 2-3 weeks and nothing. The least you could do is give some credits Bi-Weekly so some people can get a more feel for wanting to buy after more lessons instead of a few of the most basic lines in Python coding, like “print (“”)” or “print ('')”. If you do add Bi-Weekly credits it would be way better, and there are other alternatives like Mimo which I think is almost the same, but back to the main point, there should be Bi-Weekly credits for people with a free plan since the X button when the subscription prompt pops up is basically just saying “You don’t have to pay but you can’t do any lessons besides viewing them”, so it becomes useless. Please add a guaranteed way for people who want a more feel for programming credits for free, you don’t have to give them like a lot, just enough for a few lessons a week or a week and a half.

reviews.title: Paywalled.
reviews.text: You can do about one unit, which is just the print function, before being forced to pay to continue. Also, it teaches you about the “definition” and “origin” of Python instead of actual coding for about 25% of the lessons. Seemed useful and easy to grasp for the one concept it did let me learn, but other than that they just copied duolingo, pumped it full of ads and AI slop, replaced your brainpower with AI (which makes no sense if you’re trying to learn) and paywalled it. Absolute garbage, would not recommend.

reviews.title: Three day trail< thirty minutes trial period
reviews.text:
You would use energy to run your code to see if you are right during the lesson. You only get 3-5 tries to get it right and without any knowledge or prior experience going into it, it’s going to take me a while to get it right, but after learning that you can’t try after that 3-5 tries you no longer have any energy left for any other lesson which is ridiculous. 

I stagnated, see the problem, want to fix the problem, but no you have no more lives and they will never refresh for you until you pay for premium which is frankly BS.  Just a worse version of Duolingo but for coding

I hope you find this helpful to whom ever considers downloading this app.

reviews.title: Poorly Written Curriculum
reviews.text: The app ui is pretty welcoming and engaging, but thats where the puck stops for me. The beginner course curriculum is not written for someone coming in with zero experience. Much of the introductory concepts have no clear explanation. For example, one of the chapters introduces integers and decimals. It mentions that there is the existence of “floats” and the very next page has me identifying what an integer is and a float. You havent even taught me what a float is yet. I would rather not have to trial and error on the introductory concepts to learn what they mean. Otherwise there isnt much point in paying for a course. The price isnt ridiculous considering you are paying $70 annual for a developed course, but I would expect a little more thought than assumption when introducing new concepts to beginners, especially when all of the marketing is targeting that user group.
